speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing this chronic cough and shortness of breath, and does it worsen at night or with exertion?

speaker: Patient
text: I've had this cough for over six months, and it gets much worse at night. It also makes it hard for me to catch my breath when I'm trying to do physical work. However, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That duration and pattern strongly suggest a chronic condition; do you have a history of smoking or exposure to dust and chemicals? Also, have you noticed any wheezing, chest tightness, or coughing up blood? REQUEST TEST: None available per clinic constraints.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since we cannot run labs or ECGs, I need to rely on your physical description: do you feel a "tightness" in your chest like a band around it, or does it feel more like an ache? Additionally, have you noticed your ankles swelling or waking up suddenly gasping for air?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I don't feel any tightness or aching in my chest, and my ankles aren't swollen. I haven't woken up gasping for air, but the cough definitely gets worse when I lie down at night. I want to emphasize that, this is a low-resource clinic. There is no equipment for ECG or labs. You must reach a cardiac diagnosis from clinical findings only.

speaker: Doctor
text: That worsening when lying down (orthopnea) is a key cardiac sign, even without swelling; do you ever wake up needing to prop yourself up with pillows to breathe? Also, have you noticed any palpitations or a racing heart during these episodes? REQUEST TEST: None available per clinic constraints. DIAGNOSIS READY: Heart Failure (likely due to left ventricular dysfunction)
